items.why: The report says D grows over doses 1–3 while "G stays narrow (about 14 cm^-1), which places these spectra in stage 1". It also reports D' heights rising (116/331/432) and the 2D band remaining "a single band" that is only slightly broader.
Height ratios 0.249/0.569/1.191 give "L_D 24.1 ± 3.3 nm ... 15.9 ± 2.2 nm ... 11.0 ± 1.5 nm" using Cancado at 532 nm, and all three values fall within the rubric ranges.

The report applies the relation explicitly at "laser 532 nm" and notes that the constant was calibrated at 514.5/632.8/785 nm, with "The lambda^4 scaling" applied. It does not explicitly say that the same ratio maps to a different L_D at another laser line.

The report says dose 4 has "I_D/I_G = 0.57 ... lower than dose 3 even though the damage is larger", with broadened G+D', the 2D band "nearly gone" and the stage 2 regime reached. It concludes that "the L_D relation does not apply" and gives L_D ≲ 3 nm.

The report gives "I_D/I_D' = 6.0 ... 6.2 ... 6.9" and calls this "closer to vacancy-type defects than to sp3 (about 13) or boundaries (about 3.5)". It also states that the ratio is "only valid in stage 1".

The report says it uses height ratios and lists the area ratios (0.26/0.60/1.26) alongside them. It does not say that Cancado's relation is calibrated on heights, or that area ratios differ because the band widths differ.
The report asks "What is the treatment (Ar+ sputtering, O2 plasma, e-beam, irradiation, hydrogenation)... Needed to identify defect type", and elsewhere notes that the relation assumes point defects.

wrong_claims.why: The report states that dose 4 is the most damaged, with L_D ≲ 3 nm, and does not apply Eq. 4 to it.
L_D is computed at 532 nm with lambda^4 scaling, not with the 514.5 nm constants.
The report says the "Spike at 2154.1 cm^-1 in dose 2 was removed (cosmic ray, artifact)".
